advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make instrument_certified_tools assert every CERTIFIED_TOOLS entry resolved to a wrapped sync tool (or loudly log/raise on a miss) so the gauge cannot silently under-count.
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:103: `for name in CERTIFIED_TOOLS:`
src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:105: `if tool is None or getattr(tool, "is_async", False):`  followed by `continue` — a miss is silent
src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:128: `instrument_certified_tools(mcp, gauge)` — return value is None; wire_health never verifies a wrap count
ABSENCE: no error/log/assert on the miss path, so a renamed or missing certified tool leaves the gauge fail-open (in_flight stays 0 while billable work runs)
advisory.finding: instrument_certified_tools silently skips a certified tool when manager.get_tool(name) returns None or the tool is async, and wire_health never asserts that all four CERTIFIED_TOOLS were actually wrapped. If a certified tool name drifts (rename in _mcp_llm.py without updating CERTIFIED_TOOLS), or the manager returns None, that tool is never instrumented and the gauge silently under-counts — /health reports in_flight=0 while a billable op runs, and the autodeploy retire check cannot distinguish 'no ops in flight' from 'instrumentation never attached'.
advisory.suggested_fix: Track wrapped names and raise/log a McpStartupError-style error if any name in CERTIFIED_TOOLS was not found or was unexpectedly async, so a tool-name drift fails loudly instead of yielding a fail-open gauge.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Stop accepting new requests (signal uvicorn/session manager to quiesce) at the start of the SIGTERM handler, then drain the gauge, so drain converges and no new billable op starts mid-shutdown.
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:187-192: drain_then_exit(...) with `exit_fn=lambda: setattr(server, "should_exit", True)` — should_exit set only after drain returns
src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:148: `while gauge.value > 0 and monotonic() < deadline:` — waits for gauge==0 but does not stop new intake first
ABSENCE: nothing tells uvicorn to stop accepting new requests before the drain loop begins
src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:183-184: `thread = threading.Thread(...); thread.start()`
src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:194: `signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, _on_sigterm)` — installed only after the thread is already running
advisory.finding: drain_then_exit runs synchronously inside the SIGTERM handler and only sets server.should_exit=True AFTER the drain completes; uvicorn therefore keeps accepting new connections/requests for the entire (up to 1200s) drain window. A new certified op can start mid-drain, so the gauge may never reach 0 within the grace bound and the process is torn down while work is genuinely in flight.
merged_from: The HTTP serving thread is started (thread.start()) before the SIGTERM handler is installed (signal.signal), leaving a window where a SIGTERM delivered during startup runs Python's default terminate handler and kills the process without draining.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm run_http_with_grace reproduces every uvicorn/lifespan setting FastMCP's run(transport='streamable-http') applied, or reuse FastMCP's runner and only add the grace hook.
evidence: src/rebar/mcp_server.py (pre-change): `server.run(transport="streamable-http" ...)` per diff hunk
src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:174-181: config built manually from `mcp.settings.host/port/log_level` only
tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_http_transport.py:459 area: `_FakeServer.run` returns immediately — real serving/lifespan not exercised
advisory.finding: main()'s HTTP path was changed from FastMCP's server.run(transport='streamable-http') to a hand-rolled uvicorn.Server built on mcp.streamable_http_app(), replicating only host/port/log_level/timeout_graceful_shutdown. Any additional uvicorn/lifespan configuration FastMCP's own run applied (e.g. log config, other settings) is silently dropped, and the tests exercise this path with a fake uvicorn.Server so real serving parity is unverified.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make fetch-secrets.sh materialize ./mcp-static-tokens.json next to .env (always creating it, per the opcert-ed25519-key precedent) so the mcp bind-mount source exists on a fresh boot.
evidence: docker-compose.yml:362-366 comment: 'Secrets materialized by fetch-secrets.sh next to this compose file ... fetch-secrets.sh ALWAYS creates these files (empty when the slot is blank) so a missing bind-mount source can't make docker create a DIRECTORY here (bug beb1).'
docker-compose.yml:366: '- ./mcp-static-tokens.json:/run/secrets/mcp-static-tokens.json:ro'

search over infra/ for 'mcp-static-tokens' returns ONLY docker-compose.yml:350 and :366 — fetch-secrets.sh never writes it (it materializes only rebar-bot-signing-key at fetch-secrets.sh:103-109 and opcert-ed25519-key at :126-132)
ABSENCE: no `mcp-static-tokens` / `static-tokens` write anywhere in infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh
advisory.finding: The `mcp` compose service bind-mounts `./mcp-static-tokens.json` (docker-compose.yml:366) but nothing in fetch-secrets.sh materializes that file; the inline comment claiming `fetch-secrets.sh ALWAYS creates these files` is false for the new static-tokens secret. On a fresh boot the bind-mount source is absent, so Docker creates a DIRECTORY at `./mcp-static-tokens.json` (the exact bug beb1 the comment says it prevents), and the mcp container cannot read its bearer-digests file.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add an mcp-static-tokens.json materialization block to fetch-secrets.sh mirroring the opcert-ed25519-key block (fetch a JSON SSM param, write it 0600 next to .env, always create the file), and ensure the written content is a valid tokens JSON object rather than empty.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure the materialized mcp-static-tokens.json is always a valid (possibly empty-tokens-array) JSON object, or gate auth so a blank slot fails loudly once instead of crash-looping under restart: always.
evidence: docker-compose.yml environment sets REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ENABLED: "1" and REBAR_MCP_AUTH_STATIC_TOKENS_FILE: "/run/secrets/mcp-static-tokens.json" (docker-compose.yml:344-350)
docker-compose.yml mcp service: 'restart: always'

src/rebar/_mcp_auth.py:708-713 _load_static_tokens raises AuthConfigError when the file is not valid JSON; :715-718 raises when it is not a {'tokens':[...]} object — an empty file therefore fails startup
fetch-secrets.sh:123-124 notes the opcert path deliberately tolerates an empty file as a 'clear startup error'; no equivalent tolerant/valid-empty representation exists for the static-tokens JSON
advisory.finding: With REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ENABLED=1 and REBAR_MCP_AUTH_STRATEGIES=static, an empty or missing `mcp-static-tokens.json` causes AuthConfigError at startup, and because the service is `restart: always` the mcp container will crash-loop indefinitely rather than surfacing a benign degraded state — unlike the opcert key which tolerates an empty file. This is a blast-radius/idempotency hazard for the new service's boot path.
advisory.suggested_fix: When the SSM slot is blank, have fetch-secrets.sh write a valid `{"tokens": []}` document (auth enabled but no accepted tokens) so the container boots deterministically, or document that a blank slot is an intentional hard-fail and choose restart:on-failure with a bound.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that invokes a real registered certified tool via build_server and asserts /health's in_flight reflects the wrapped fn (not gauge.track directly).
evidence: instrument_certified_tools reads real internals: src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:100 `manager = getattr(mcp, "_tool_manager", None)` and :104 `tool = manager.get_tool(name)` and :107 `tool.fn = _wrap_tool_fn(...)`
test uses a fake mirror: tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_http_transport.py:373 `manager = SimpleNamespace(get_tool=lambda n: tools.get(n))` and :374 `mcp = SimpleNamespace(_tool_manager=manager)`

test_health_reports_in_flight_gauge_idle_inflight_and_contrast builds a real server but manipulates the gauge directly (`with gauge.track("review_plan")`) instead of invoking a registered tool, so no test connects build_server/wire_health -> real tool manager -> gauge -> /health
advisory.finding: No test drives a REAL registered certified tool through the wired-up server to prove instrument_certified_tools actually moves the gauge; the sole instrumentation test builds a SimpleNamespace(_tool_manager=..., get_tool=..., tool.fn/is_async) that hand-mirrors FastMCP's internal object graph, so the production path's dependence on those exact internals (`mcp._tool_manager`, `manager.get_tool`, `tool.fn`, `tool.is_async`) is never verified against the real object. If FastMCP renames/reshapes any of these, instrument_certified_tools silently no-ops in production while every unit test stays green.
scenarios: FastMCP upgrade renames _tool_manager or the tool.fn/is_async attributes; instrumentation becomes a no-op but tests pass

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Exercise /health inflight by invoking the instrumented tool fn rather than calling gauge.track() directly in the test.
evidence: inflight case bypasses the wrapper: `with gauge.track("review_plan"):` then `inflight = client.get("/health").json()`
contrast case likewise: `with gauge.track("list_tickets"):` — this exercises gauge.track's CERTIFIED_TOOLS gate, not the tool wrapping added at src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:107
advisory.finding: The /health inflight assertion re-derives the gauge state with gauge.track() rather than driving the production instrumentation path; the endpoint test therefore cannot detect a regression in _wrap_tool_fn / instrument_certified_tools (only in gauge.value + JSON serialization).
scenarios: _wrap_tool_fn stops calling gauge.track (e.g. name binding bug); this endpoint test still passes because it calls gauge.track itself

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add cases for instrument_certified_tools with an is_async=True tool, a missing tool, and a None _tool_manager.
evidence: added guards: src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:101 `if manager is None: return`, :105 `if tool is None or getattr(tool, "is_async", False): continue`
tests only pass is_async=False stubs: tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_http_transport.py:370-371 `SimpleNamespace(fn=..., is_async=False)`
ABSENCE: search of the test file for `is_async` returns only the two False-valued stub constructions; no case with is_async=True, no None-tool case, no None-manager case
advisory.finding: The added skip/guard branches in instrument_certified_tools are untested for their named inputs: an async certified tool (`is_async=True`) must be left untouched, a missing tool (`get_tool returns None`) must be skipped, and a server with no `_tool_manager` (`manager is None`) must return without error. All three are added lines with concrete violating inputs and no test.
scenarios: A FastMCP build registers a certified tool as async; the untested skip must preserve it — if _wrap_tool_fn wrongly wrapped it (sync wrapper over a coroutine fn) the server would break, but no test guards the skip
